notes: Windows config provider apply requires current source and candidate SHA256, a new backup and both --confirm-apply and --confirm-offline. Only the Provider domain may change. It refuses unchanged selection, invalid input, source drift, candidate drift, unrelated domains, read-only source, existing file owners, hard links, unsafe parents, oversize data and existing backup

The exact source/candidate handles and directory pins remain held. New backup bytes are synchronized and read back before source mutation. Source is overwritten, length-adjusted, synchronized and read back on the original held handle. This preserves identity/ACLs but is non-atomic and not power-loss safe; exclusive Windows data handles do not prove every configured daemon is stopped

Twenty real CLI scenarios include provider-only save, restoring a prior valid provider, full corrupt-source recovery, bad recovery input, no confirmations, held inputs, hard links, read-only source/candidate, oversized candidate and missing backup parent. Ten injected I/O failures plus a pre-write failure validate source uncertainty and no automatic rollback

Three independent child exits occur after verified backup, after twelve source bytes and after source synchronization. Parent reopens files, verifies exact original backup and retained residue, then explicitly restores a valid full configuration while preserving the residue in another new file. Process exit is not a physical-power-failure test

Restore is a separately confirmed full-snapshot operation, not a provider-only merge. It can recover an invalid source but requires a valid bounded reviewed candidate, both current digests and a new residue backup. All source-write uncertainties remain unknown; no retry, automatic rollback, daemon restart, environment overlay or secret resolution occurs

with_provider_model changes only an explicitly configured active provider model and revalidates the whole snapshot. claw-platform native-config is an optional shared inspection/preparation service reused by CLI and Slint. Windows source/output are exclusive for operation lifetime; new candidate is read back and source is never mutated. No new provider authentication or catalogue claim is inferred. Unix/macOS prepare uses existing sandbox guarantees; apply/restore explicitly reject unsupported platforms before mutation

Slint adds a local source/path inspection and exact current-page model menu with full long-ID preview and a new candidate destination. Provider kind and current model must match the observed catalogue, but Gateway file/account/endpoint association is not proven and must be independently reviewed. There is no graphical online switch or direct apply button

Desktop file work is independent of Gateway RPC and runs off the UI thread. One local task is admitted, started tasks are drained on normal shutdown, generation reset preserves local pending/results, and lost UI result queues release busy state with explicit outcome unknown. Stale sequence, connection, page or source hash cannot silently redirect a candidate. Candidate files are never deleted on an uncertain result

Actual Slint callback-to-controller-to-file test verifies inspection and candidate creation without a Gateway connection, preserves source and rejects stale selection after disconnect. Software pixels at 1080x720 and 720x520 cover 252-byte model ID, wrapping preview, disabled controls and clearing a hidden editor's old index. These are not physical user/platform acceptance
